subject: Unit economics check-in — projected monthly corridor & PO gating
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unit economics check-in — projected monthly corridor & PO gating

Hi Sam — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so procurement has a clean handoff.

Call highlights (30m):
- FluxHealth primary workload: real-time summarization + personalization scoring for notifications; median prompt length ~850 tokens, tail spikes to ~3k tokens.
- Expected query volume: 200K — 1.2M tokens/month (estimate) across two environments (prod / staging).
- Success metric: maintain p50 latency < 200ms for 1k-token requests; cost target to keep infra ops under $/1M tokens that aligns with their finance guardrails.

Preliminary cost band we discussed:
- Conservative pilot corridor: $8k — $18k / month (approx. 200K — 450K tokens)
- Scale corridor: $18k — $40k / month (450K — 1.2M tokens)
- Unit economics target we used on the call: ~$300 per 1M tokens (this is illustrative; final depends on batching, KV cache, and reserved capacity).

Procurement gating notes:
- Standard PO required for commitments >= $25k/month.
- Below $25k/month can run on invoice/credit-card pilot (30–90 day window).
- SOC2 evidence, pricing worksheet, and SOW draft attached for procurement.

Next steps (action owners):
1) I will share a compact rate worksheet and SOW draft (attached) — Evelyn (done).
2) Sam/Procurement to confirm preferred procurement path (PO vs credit card pilot) and target decision date — Sam.
3) If PO: procurement to send vendor onboarding questionnaire; Redwood to return with SOC2 summary & standard terms — Vanessa/Karthik.

Would you be able to confirm procurement preference and an approximate internal sign date by Friday, Oct 22? If useful, we can provide a one-page pilot economics example mapped to their expected monthly volumes.

Thanks — enjoyed the demo.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 (415) 555-0182

Evelyn — thanks for the recap and for sending the materials. A few quick clarifications from procurement and product: 

- Procurement: if we go the PO route, lead time is typically 3–4 weeks (legal review + vendor setup). If we do a CC pilot, finance wants a strict 60-day cap on pilot spend.
- Product: is the ~$300 / 1M tokens line item inclusive of model licensing or strictly inference runtime? We need to map to our internal cost centers.

Can you give a 1-page sketch showing: (A) monthly spend vs tokens table for 3 buckets (250K, 600K, 1.1M tokens), and (B) what changes if we apply a reserved pool discount (15%) vs on-demand? That will speed alignment with finance.

Also cc'ing procurement (procure@fluxhealth.com) — they'll want SOC2 and an expected SOW length and start date.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Delgado
Head of Product | FluxHealth
sam@fluxhealth.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Delgado <sam@fluxhealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Unit economics check-in — projected monthly corridor & PO gating

Hi Sam — thanks for the questions and for looping procurement in. Picking up the two asks: cost sketch and what changes with reserved pool discounts. See below — I attached a tidy worksheet that maps the three token buckets you requested.

Short answers up front:
- The ~$300 / 1M tokens is an illustrative blended inference runtime price that assumes: standard quantized model (v2.1), modest batching (20–40ms aggregation), and prefix caching on warm flows. Model licensing (if you opt for a premium model variant) would be an incremental line item — not included in the base runtime number.
- Reserved pool discount: we can offer 15% on the token unit rate for a 3-month reserved commit at the mid corridor ($18k+/month), and larger commits (6+ months) scale to 20% depending on GPU-class commitment.

High level table (excerpt from attached sheet):
- 250K tokens / month -> Baseline: $75 / month (est.) [note: we present per-1M scaled: $300/1M so 0.25*300 = $75]
- 600K tokens / month -> Baseline: $180 / month
- 1.1M tokens / month -> Baseline: $330 / month

With 15% reserved discount: multiply baseline by 0.85. Example: 1.1M -> ~$281 / month.

Procurement path options: 
1) Credit-card pilot (recommended short path): up to $25k/month, 60-day cap, no PO required.
2) PO / Vendor onboarding: vendor form + standard redlines; timeline 2–4 weeks depending on legal bandwidth.

Attachments included: FluxHealth_Rate_worksheet.xlsx (token vs spend table + reserved-discount scenarios), SOW_Draft_v2.pdf (30-day pilot option and escalation clause), SOC2_summary.pdf (summary and link to full report upon NDA).

Action items:
- Sam/Procurement: confirm pilot path (CC pilot vs PO) and whether finance prefers modeling costs monthly as run-rate or as committed reserve.
- Evelyn: follow up with a 1-page pilot economics callout for Sam to share with Finance (Evelyn to send by EOD Oct 21).

If you want, Priyom and I can jump on a 20min call with finance to walk through the worksheet — we have availability Fri Oct 22 10–11am or Mon Oct 25 afternoon.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
